subject: Sleep, Anxiety, and the Empty-Nest Brain: Why Movement and Community Are Biological Levers
script: From Agewell Brief: Sleep, Anxiety, and the Empty-Nest Brain: Why Movement and Community Are Biological Levers. A new cross-sectional study of 6,106 Chinese empty-nest elders finds poor sleep triples anxiety risk—and reveals how physical exercise and social participation act as biological mediators. Sleep is not a passive off-switch. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
